title: The Atom's Family Tree
intro: This quiz checks what you learned about atomic number, mass number, and isotopes.

questions.prompt: What does the atomic number of an element tell us?
questions.explanation: Atomic number tells us the number of protons in an atom’s nucleus.

questions.prompt: How is the mass number of an atom calculated?
questions.explanation: Mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

questions.prompt: An atom has 8 protons and 9 neutrons. What is its mass number?

choices: Atoms of different elements with the same number of neutrons
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of protons
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
questions.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.

questions.prompt: Why is chlorine's average atomic mass about 35.5 instead of a whole number?
choices: Chlorine has different isotopes with different masses and natural abundances
Chlorine has the same number of protons and neutrons
Chlorine's mass number changes every day
questions.explanation: Average atomic mass reflects chlorine’s isotopes and their natural abundances, so it is not a whole number.
